payload.author: SirHegel
payload.title: Fall back to 'pipx' when argv[0] is not pipx

payload.author: SirHegel
payload.body:
Closing — #2007 predates this by five days and fixes #2005 more surgically: it threads an explicit `prog` through `get_command_parser()` so only `build_parser()` overrides it, leaving `prog_name()` alone.

One difference worth having on record, since the two are not equivalent in scope. #2007 fixes the docs build. This one changed `prog_name()` itself to fall back to `"pipx"` whenever `argv[0]` is neither a `pipx*` binary nor `__main__.py`, which also covers any *other* host process that imports the parser — a test runner, an embedding tool. Whether that wider behaviour is wanted is a design call, not a bug fix, so #2007 is the right shape for this issue.

Sorry for the duplicate; I filtered #2005 on having no assignee and no comments and did not check for a PR already referencing it.

payload.title: 🐛 fix: don't crash scanning a foreign binary in the bin dir

payload.author: gaborbernat
payload.body:
Thanks for picking this up. Three PRs arrived for #1965, so I have folded them into #1970 and am closing this one in favour of that. The commit credits you as a co-author.

One note that might help next time. The `b"\xff\xfe"` payload holds no `#!`, so the marker search found nothing and the assertion passed against unpatched `main`, which means the test went green without the fix in place. A regression test earns its keep by failing first, so it is worth reverting `src/` and watching it go red before opening the PR. #1970 drives the same cases through the public scan on payloads that carry a marker, and patches `can_symlink` so the parse runs off Windows too.

Thanks again for the time you put in. 🙏

payload.author: dchaudhari7177
payload.title: fix: don't crash on a foreign executable in the pipx bin directory

payload.author: gaborbernat
payload.body:
Thank you for this one. Noticing that a decoded path holding a NUL still reaches `stat` and raises `ValueError` is the piece that made the fix complete. The report only covers the Windows crash, and catching `UnicodeDecodeError` on its own would have left that second one live on Linux and macOS. Reaching for `ValueError` to cover both is the right call.

Three PRs arrived for #1965, so I have folded them into #1970 and am closing this one in favour of that. The tests there patch `can_symlink` as well, since it returns `True` on every non-Windows platform and the symlink branch would otherwise skip the parse outside the Windows jobs.

The commit credits you as a co-author. Thanks for digging past the traceback. 🙏

payload.author: alberto743
payload.title: fix: don't crash on non-UTF8 shebang in foreign bin-dir executables

payload.author: alberto743
payload.body: here is the outcome of the tests: https://github.com/alberto743/pipx/actions/runs/29617910282

payload.author: gaborbernat
payload.body:
Thank you for this, and for the write-up in particular. Pinning the crash on Windows decoding filesystem bytes with `surrogatepass` where POSIX uses `surrogateescape` is the right root cause, and the final fix rests on it.

Three PRs arrived for #1965, so I have folded them into #1970 and am closing this one in favour of that. #1970 widens the guard to `ValueError` rather than `UnicodeDecodeError`, which also covers a second crash the report does not mention: off Windows `os.fsdecode` escapes the bad bytes instead of raising, but a decoded path holding a NUL still reaches `stat`.

The commit credits you as a co-author. Thanks again for the careful diagnosis. 🙏

That's exciting, Bernát! Thank you for working on this. One question about the following…

> Pass `--json` to read the installed and available versions in a script.

Does that mean that in the current implementation, `pipx list --outdated` will *not* show both the installed and available version numbers? I ask because it seems like that would be useful information to have in the non-JSON view. For example, it seems Pip shows this information when running `pip list --outdated`:

```
~ ➤ python -m pip list --outdated

Package Version Latest Type
------- ------- ------ -----
pip     26.0.1  26.1.2 wheel
```

Perhaps I'm misunderstanding the documentation in the PR, and if so, my apologies! Otherwise, is there some specific reason not to include the version number information in the non-JSON view?

payload.author: marko1olo
payload.body:
Follow-up pushed in `444776e` for the pre-commit.ci mypy failure.

What changed:

- added the new test fixture `testdata/test_package_specifier/local_manpage/setup.py` to the same mypy hook exclude pattern as the existing `local_extras/setup.py` fixture
- made the editable project `setup.py` AST inspection type-safe by narrowing to `ast.Call` before reading `.keywords`
- typed the normalized `data_files` iterator input/items to avoid mypy's incorrect inferred assignment/unreachable path

Checks run locally:

```text
uv run --with ruff ruff check src\pipx\venv_inspect.py
uv run --with ruff ruff format --check src\pipx\venv_inspect.py
uv run --with mypy python -m mypy src\pipx\venv_inspect.py --warn-unused-ignores --strict-equality --no-implicit-optional --check-untyped-defs
uv run --with pre-commit pre-commit run mypy --files testdata\test_package_specifier\local_manpage\setup.py
git diff --check
```

The focused editable-install pytest hung locally while pip was trying to build the fixture environment from the local package cache, so I killed that local run and did not count it as validation. The original behavior tests are unchanged from the previous PR version; this push only addresses the mypy/pre-commit.ci blocker.

payload.author: bobo-xxx
payload.body: Confirmed: this change breaks checksum validation. In _unpack(), the computed checksum is "sha256:" + hexdigest, compared against expected_checksum. If expected_checksum is just the raw hash (stripped of prefix), the comparison ALWAYS fails. The original code is correct — digests must retain the sha256: prefix. Please close or revert this PR.

payload.author: bobo-xxx
payload.body: Closing — I was wrong. The fix is correct. After deeper analysis: resolve_python_version() returns 2 values (full_version, (download_link, digest)) and the digest contains 'sha256:HASH'. The _unpack() function correctly compares 'sha256:' + hexdigest against the stored digest. The original code is correct. Sorry for the noise.
